title: Turkish Airlines 452
summary: Turkish Airlines Flight 452 crashed into Karatepe Hill near Isparta after the first officer mistook city lights of Isparta for the runway at Antalya. The pilots attempted visual flight at night instead of using instruments, mistaking dark mountains for the Mediterranean Sea. The aircraft descended too early and crashed into a hill.
probable_cause: Pilot error: the first officer mistook the city lights of Isparta for the runway of Antalya and the aircraft descended too early. The pilots attempted visual flight instead of required instrumental flight at night.

factors.evidence: The pilots mistook the city lights of Isparta for those of Antalya and the dark area ahead for the Mediterranean Sea.
The pilots were trying to fly visually, instead of instrumental flight, which was required at night.
First Officer Soğangöz responded to the controller's warning: 'Should I believe you, or my eyes?'.
The accident occurred at night when external visual references were degraded.
The aircraft crashed its right wing in a hill at Karatepe and bounced off to the other side of the valley and disintegrated.

events.text: The pilots reported that they could see the lights of the city, while the plane was around 100 km north of it.
When the pilots confirmed they had the runway in sight, the controller at Antalya notified them that he couldn't see them.
Captain Topçuoğlu, who was in the passenger cabin, returned to the cockpit after realizing that something was wrong at an altitude of 150 m.
The aircraft crashed its right wing in a hill, bounced off to the other side of the valley and disintegrated at Karatepe.
